primitives.name: Offensive Run Path Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: 108 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS Diagram 8 shows still another phase of the runninggame, where a rusher runs around behind the quarter, taking the ball from him on the run and making for DIAGRAM 8.
primitives.assumptions: Linear motion of rusher relative to quarterback, constant velocity during transition phase.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rusher's trajectory intersects with quarterback's path at time t=0.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a kinematic trajectory problem in 2D space with initial conditions defined by player positions.
layer2.telemetry: Player displacement vectors measured via tracking data

primitives.name: Defensive Alignment Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: ponents in facing the runninggame, and that is according to diagram 10.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_defense': 'probability density function over defensive alignment (dimensionless)', 'θ': 'angle of defensive line orientation (radians)', 'σ': 'standard deviation of alignment uncertainty (radians)'}
primitives.assumptions: Defensive alignment follows Gaussian distribution centered on expected run direction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed run direction deviates beyond 2σ threshold from expected.

layer2.mapping: Kernel density estimation derived from historical defensive formations under similar offensive setups.
layer2.telemetry: Defensive alignment angles recorded per play

primitives.name: Formation Transition Logic
primitives.verbatim_quote: Let us now consider the formation of the opposing side during DIAGRAM 9.
primitives.assumptions: Formation changes based on cumulative risk assessment of continuing run attempt versus kicking.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R > 20 yards or progress < 5 yards after two attempts.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to Markov decision process with discrete states representing formation configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Play outcome classification into run/kick categories
